text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The Group of 24 industrial nations approved in Brussels some $400 million support for Bulgaria's balance of payments to be extended by the World Bank and the European Union.

-- Bulgaria's Chief Prosecutor's Office had launched an investigation against six bankers of bankrupt state owned Mineralbank on suspected wrongdoing in extending credits worth some 100 billion levs. @
-- France has granted 5,000 tonnes of wheat to Bulgaria, Agriculture minister Roumen Hristov said.

-- The leader of the Bulgarian Socialist Party (BSP) Georgi Parvanov called for transparency in the structural reforms implemented by the interim cabinet at a meeting with the President Petar Stoyanov. @

-- Bulgaria and Russia agreed on the terms of the intergovernmental agreement on transiting Russian natural gas via Bulgaria. Prime minister Stefan Sofianski was expected to sign the agreement with Russia's Prime minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on April 11 in Moscow.
-- Bulgaria's Industry ministry is planning to sell 76 state companies by year-end with proceeds expected to total 26 billion levs, deputy Industry minister Edit Getova said.
-- Bulgaria is expected to sell 48 hotels at the northern Black Sea resort Zlatni Piasatzi by the year-end, Tourist Committee chairman Roumen Draganov said. @
-- The Sofia City Court declared the Private Agricultural and Investment Bank insolvent at the request of the Bulgarian National Bank.
-- The Bulgarian lev is expected to be pegged at 2,000 per dollar if a currency board system is introduced in the country in June, experts from the Bulgarian Academy of Sciences said.
-- Monthly inflation for March is expected at 10 percent under estimates by the National Statistics Institute.
-- Bulgaria's Prime minister Stefan Sofianski is expected to sign a bilateral trade liberalisation accord with Russia's Prime minister Viktor Chernomyrdin by the end of the week.

-- Bulgaria's caretaker cabinet is expected to raise central heating prices by eight percent from May 1 in line with pledges made to the International Monetary Fund. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
